paragraphs.zh: 3. The process for preparation of mesotrione as claimed in claim 1, wherein the reaction of NMSBA of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione is carried out in presence of N, N′-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and a solvent.
paragraphs.en: 3. The process for preparation of mesotrione as claimed in claim 1, wherein the reaction of NMSBA of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione is carried out in presence of N, N′-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and a solvent.
paragraphs.notes: Claim 3. Dependent: 'as claimed in claim 1'. This is the FIRST entry on the page and it is NOT a continuation: the page opens with the printed numeral '3.' at the top of the body block and the claim runs to a full stop within the page, so claim 2 closed on p19 and nothing is carried over the top boundary. Claim number kept at the start of the text as instructed; marker is null because a claim is not a numbered paragraph. The printed page sets a wide justification gap between '3.' and 'The'; transcribed as one space. The glyph after the second N is a PRIME (U+2032), a straight right-leaning tick, checked at 9x magnification; it is not an ASCII apostrophe and not a curly quote. Note the printed 'N, N' has a space after the comma. Spelling here is the abbreviation NMSBA only, so neither the ph nor the f spelling appears in this claim.

paragraphs.zh: 4. The process for preparation of mesotrione as claimed in claim 1, wherein the conversion of the enol ester of formula (II) to mesotrione of formula (I) comprises reaction of the enol ester of formula (II) with sodium cyanide in presence of a base and a solvent to produce mesotrione of formula (I).
paragraphs.en: 4. The process for preparation of mesotrione as claimed in claim 1, wherein the conversion of the enol ester of formula (II) to mesotrione of formula (I) comprises reaction of the enol ester of formula (II) with sodium cyanide in presence of a base and a solvent to produce mesotrione of formula (I).
paragraphs.notes: Claim 4. Dependent: 'as claimed in claim 1'. Carries no quantity, range, temperature or time: the conditions are named only qualitatively as 'sodium cyanide in presence of a base and a solvent'. Formula numbers (I) and (II) are printed with parentheses in the claim text. The left-margin line number 5 sits beside this claim's second line and is furniture, excluded from the text.

paragraphs.zh: 5. A process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) by oxidizing 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium oxide as a catalyst.
paragraphs.en: 5. A process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) by oxidizing 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium oxide as a catalyst.
paragraphs.notes: Claim 5. INDEPENDENT: it opens 'A process for preparation of', not 'The process ... as claimed in', so it does not depend on claim 1 or on anything else on this page. It is the second independent claim of the set. Brief section 8 is confirmed exactly here: one sentence prints BOTH spellings, '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid' with a ph and '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene' with an f, on consecutive printed lines. Both are transcribed as printed and NOT normalised. Conditions are qualitative only, 'an oxidant' and 'ruthenium oxide as a catalyst', with no quantity, ratio, temperature or time. The left-margin line number 10 sits beside this claim's third line. The scheme in drawings[0] is printed immediately below this claim.

paragraphs.zh: 6. The process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) as claimed in claim 5, wherein the oxidant is sodium hypochlorite.
paragraphs.en: 6. The process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) as claimed in claim 5, wherein the oxidant is sodium hypochlorite.
paragraphs.notes: Claim 6. Dependent: 'as claimed in claim 5'. It is the only claim on the page that names a specific reagent, sodium hypochlorite, and it names it without any quantity or concentration. Spelling here is the ph form, 'methylsulphonyl'.

paragraphs.zh: 7. A process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione.
paragraphs.en: 7. A process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione.
paragraphs.notes: Claim 7. INDEPENDENT: it opens 'A process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of', so it does not depend on any earlier claim. It is the third independent claim of the set. Its subject matter is the same coupling that dependent claim 3 conditions, but claim 3 hangs off claim 1 while claim 7 stands alone; a later pass needs both facts. Spelling is the ph form. '1,3-cyclohexanedione' is printed with no space after the comma. The left-margin line number 15 sits beside this claim's second line. The scheme in drawings[1] is printed immediately below this claim.

paragraphs.zh: 8. The process for preparation of an enol ester as claimed in claim 7, wherein the reaction is carried out in presence of N, N′-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and a solvent.
paragraphs.en: 8. The process for preparation of an enol ester as claimed in claim 7, wherein the reaction is carried out in presence of N, N′-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and a solvent.
paragraphs.notes: Claim 8. Dependent: 'as claimed in claim 7'. This is the LAST entry on the page and it is COMPLETE, closing with a full stop after 'and a solvent.'; the page does not end mid-sentence, so nothing is carried over onto p21 from this claim and claim 9 must begin on p21. Same prime glyph (U+2032) after the second N as in claim 3, and the same space after the comma in 'N, N'. Conditions qualitative only, no quantity or range. Last inked row on the page is 2062 of 2338 and every band below it is blank, which is why footer is the empty string.

drawings.notes: One left-to-right single-arrow scheme printed between claim 5 and claim 6, occupying rows 854 to 1227 of the page. It is the SAME scheme already recorded on p15, between the two paragraphs there whose numbers are 46 and 47 (written here without brackets on purpose, so that no marker-shaped string appears in this file for a page that has none), reprinted here inside the claims, and my reading of it was made from this page before comparing: same two structures, same 'Oxidant / RuO2' above the arrow, same labels. Ring positions were read off the drawn hexagons, not inferred. Both benzene rings are drawn vertex-up: the top vertex carries CH3 (left structure) or the C(=O)OH group (right structure), the upper-right vertex carries NO2, and the bottom vertex, para to the top one, carries the SO2 whose H3C is written to its lower left. The two printed labels read 'Formula IV' (left) and 'Formula III' (right); both roman numerals were re-checked at 8x because the degraded ink makes II, III and IV easy to confuse, and both are certain. Note that the drawing labels print the numeral WITHOUT parentheses, 'Formula IV', while the claim text beside them writes 'formula (IV)' with parentheses. Every stroke of the scheme is broken dotted ink from the bitonal scan, per brief section 9; the arrow looks dashed on the page but is a degraded solid line with one solid arrowhead and is recorded as solid. Nothing at all is printed below the arrow.

drawings.notes: One left-to-right single-arrow scheme printed between claim 7 and claim 8, occupying rows 1595 to 1902. Two reactants are drawn to the left of the arrow joined by a printed '+', and one product to the right. The arrow is COMPLETELY BARE: nothing is printed above it and nothing below it, verified at 4x over the whole span between the middle structure and the product. The middle structure, 1,3-cyclohexanedione, carries NO printed label; only the first and third structures are labelled, 'Formula III' and 'Formula II' respectively, again without parentheses where the claim text uses them. Ring positions read off the drawings. In the product the benzene ring is drawn tilted rather than vertex-up: the vertex bearing the ester carbonyl is at the upper right, the NO2 vertex is the one adjacent to it at the top, and the H3C-SO2 vertex is two further round on the lower left, which is C4 counting from the carbonyl carbon as C1. The cyclohexenone ring of the product is drawn with its ketone on the top vertex, a C=C along the left edge, and the ester oxygen on the lower-left vertex, so the enol oxygen and the ketone are 1,3 to each other; that is the enol ester of 1,3-cyclohexanedione and not the 1,2 isomer. In this product the methylsulfonyl group is drawn differently from the first scheme, as H3C bonded to an S with a subscript O2 written below the S, rather than as the single 'SO2' label used in the first scheme; both denote the same methylsulfonyl group and the difference is one of drawing style, recorded here rather than normalised away. Same broken dotted ink and same degraded-solid arrow as the first scheme. Formula masses of the four drawn structures are consistent with the claimed condensation, 245 plus 112 minus 18 equals 339, which is a cross-check on the drawings and not a source for any of them.

discrepancies.what: The scheme under claim 5 names the oxidant only generically while claim 6, printed immediately below the same scheme, names a specific one. This is the same disagreement the brief records on p15, recurring in the claims.
discrepancies.drawing_says: 'Oxidant / RuO2' above the arrow, the only text on it. The actual oxidant is left unnamed, and the reagent and the catalyst are run together on one line separated by a slash so the drawing does not distinguish which is which.
discrepancies.text_says: Claim 5 asks for 'an oxidant in presence of ruthenium oxide as a catalyst'; claim 6 then fixes 'the oxidant is sodium hypochlorite', which appears nowhere on the drawing.

discrepancies.what: The scheme under claim 7 draws the coupling with a bare arrow, while both claim 3 and claim 8 make a coupling agent and a solvent essential to it.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Nothing above the arrow and nothing below it: no coupling agent, no solvent, no temperature, no time. Only the two reactants, the '+' and the product are drawn.
discrepancies.text_says: Claim 3 and claim 8 both require the reaction to be 'carried out in presence of N, N′-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and a solvent'.

discrepancies.what: The page contradicts itself on the spelling of the methylsulfonyl moiety, twice within claim 5's single sentence and then consistently one way afterwards. Recorded, not resolved.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The drawings carry no spelled-out name at all, only 'Formula IV', 'Formula III', 'Formula II' and the graphical SO2 / S-O2 labels, so they cannot arbitrate the spelling.
discrepancies.text_says: Claim 5 prints '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid' with a ph and '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene' with an f, on consecutive lines of one sentence. Claims 6 and 7 then use the ph form only. Both forms are transcribed exactly as printed and neither has been normalised.

discrepancies.what: Claim 3 and claim 7 claim the same transformation at different dependencies, which a later pass must not collapse.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Only one drawing of this coupling is printed, under claim 7.
discrepancies.text_says: Claim 3 conditions the NMSBA plus 1,3-cyclohexanedione reaction as a dependent of claim 1, while claim 7 claims the same reaction as a standalone independent claim and claim 8 then adds the identical N, N′-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and solvent condition to it.
